article_title: Facilitating Flexible Problem Solving: A Cognitive Load Perspective
citation: Slava Kalyuga, Alexander Renkl, Fred Paas. (2010). Facilitating Flexible Problem Solving: A Cognitive Load Perspective. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-010-9132-9
title: Function-Process-Structure (FPS) schema as a generalized framework for technical domains
description: The FPS schema is a triarchic generalized schema for technical knowledge: a technical object is characterized by its functions (what it is for), the natural processes utilized in its operation (how it operates), and its internal structure (what it consists of). Understanding means establishing mental connections between these components, each describable at multiple levels of generality. The paper states the framework "provides a generalized schema that can be used as a deep explanatory principle that may allow effective reasoning about complex systems" and captures expert-novice differences, with novices focusing on perceptually available structural components while experts organize knowledge around processes and functions.
requirements: Learners must establish mental connections between the function, process, and structure components; basic concepts and routine procedures need to be well automated to release cognitive resources
constraints: Developed for technical domains; related but distinct approaches such as the structure-behaviour-function framework exist
target_learners: novices learning about technical devices and systems
target_learning_goals: deep understanding of complex technical systems and flexible reasoning about them
examples: The paper illustrates levels of generality with an air-conditioning system whose function can be described from lowering room temperature down to refrigerant phase transformation
key_sources: Slava Kalyuga, Alexander Renkl, Fred Paas. (2010). Facilitating Flexible Problem Solving: A Cognitive Load Perspective. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-010-9132-9
